title: bagu-trainer track manifest (track.yaml)
description: Design v0.3 §4.2. A track is a supply-chain package that runs executable code on the learner's machine, so track.yaml is split into inert `manifest` (declarative metadata the platform only reads) and executable `runtime` (the attack surface). `trust_level` is first-class: self | verified | community (§4.6, §13).

trust_level.description: Supply-chain trust tier (§13). self = self-hosted/authored, trusted by default. verified = maintainer-endorsed + digest-pinned + passed CI admission. community = third-party, NOT fully trusted by default; primary defense is disclosure + review + digest-pinning + reputation, sandbox is defense-in-depth only.

manifest.description: INERT declarative metadata. The platform reads this to render the board and health-check the environment; it NEVER executes anything here.

requires.description: Learner-device prerequisites (declared only; the platform health-checks against them, it does not auto-install).

skeleton_repo.description: Skeleton the learner starts from (one branch per stage).

stages.description: Progressive stages; each ticket expresses its own dependencies via progression.prerequisites.

runtime.description: EXECUTABLE entry points (the supply-chain attack surface — these really run on the learner's machine). Per §4.6 every executable entry must be covered by digest_pin.

compose.description: docker-compose path (e.g. mysql:8.0@13306 + redis:7@16379, off default ports).

protected_paths.description: The JUDGED SURFACE (§11.3): paths whose contents the verdict depends on — canonical tests, build config, fixtures, the track's own infra. Any learner change to one of them FAILS the acceptance gate outright. This is the cheap hard gate that stands in for runtime test injection (§7.3) until that lands: while the canonical tests still live inside the learner's repo, declaring them here is what keeps 'edit the test' from being a free pass. Globs allowed (e.g. ./src/test/ or ./**/pom.xml).

digest_pin.description: Pinned digests for executable dependencies, preventing supply-chain drift. Keys name the dependency (mysql/redis/...), values are sha256:... digests.

license.description: Content-repo license (MIT in the three-layer topology, §6.7).

ci.description: Admission gate command, e.g. `paper validate-track` (§4.6, CI-enforced).

signed_by.description: Maintainer endorsements; required to promote a track to `verified`.
